EXONDYS 51 was studied in a double-blind, placebo-controlled study for 24 weeks (Study 1), followed by an open label extension (Study 2). In Study 1, 12 patients were randomized to receive weekly intravenous infusions of EXONDYS 51 (n=8) or placebo (n=4) for 24 weeks.

phase.text: Not specified as a phase; approval was based primarily on a post hoc comparison of 12 treated DMD patients to 13 external untreated controls.

citations.quote: The Applicant is proposing approval based primarily on a post hoc comparison of 12 patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping from the open-label portion of a single study (Study 201/202) to 13 patients from an external untreated control group.

design.text: Study 1: 24-week double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial, then open-label extension Study 2 (up to 208 weeks) compared to an external control group; Study 3: open-label, 48-week single-arm study with paired baseline/Week 48 muscle biopsies.

citations.quote: EXONDYS 51 was studied in a double-blind, placebo-controlled study for 24 weeks (Study 1), followed by an open label extension (Study 2). In Study 1, 12 patients were randomized to receive weekly intravenous infusions of EXONDYS 51 (n=8) or placebo (n=4) for 24 weeks. All 12 patients continued in Study 2 and received open-label EXONDYS 51 weekly for up to 208 weeks.
In Study 3, 13 patients were treated with open-label EXONDYS 51 (30 mg/kg) weekly for 48 weeks and had a muscle biopsy at baseline and after 48 weeks of treatment.

population.text: Patients with a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene amenable to exon 51 skipping, on stable corticosteroids; mean age 9.4 years in Study 1 and 8.9 years in Study 3.

citations.quote: Patients had a mean age of 9.4 years, a mean 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) at baseline of 363 meters, and were on a stable dose of corticosteroids for at least 6 months.
Patients had a mean age of 8.9 years and were on a stable dose of corticosteroids for at least 6 months.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint in Study 1 was dystrophin production; the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) was assessed as a clinical outcome measure.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was dystrophin production; a clinical outcome measure, the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), was also assessed.

n.text: Study 1: 12 patients randomized (EXONDYS 51 30 mg/kg n=4, 50 mg/kg n=4, placebo n=4); Study 3: 13 patients treated, 12 evaluable.

citations.quote: In Study 1, patients were randomized to receive weekly infusions of EXONDYS 51 (30 mg/kg, n=4); EXONDYS 51 (50 mg/kg, n=4), or placebo (n=4) for 24 weeks.
In Study 3, 13 patients were treated with open-label EXONDYS 51 (30 mg/kg) weekly for 48 weeks and had a muscle biopsy at baseline and after 48 weeks of treatment.

result.text: No significant difference in 6MWD change between EXONDYS 51 and placebo. In Study 3, mean dystrophin was 0.16% of normal before treatment and 0.44% after 48 weeks (p < 0.05); median increase 0.1% (mean change p=0.008). In Study 2, average dystrophin was 0.93% of normal after 180 weeks and Study 2 failed to show clinical benefit vs the external control.

citations.quote: There was no significant difference in change in 6MWD between patients treated with EXONDYS 51 and those treated with placebo.

the pre-treatment dystrophin level was 0.16\% \pm 0.12\% (mean \pm standard deviation) of the dystrophin level in a healthy subject and 0.44\% \pm 0.43\% after 48 weeks of treatment with EXONDYS 51 (p < 0.05). The median increase after 48 weeks was 0.1%.

Study 2 failed to provide evidence of a clinical benefit of EXONDYS 51 compared to the external control group. The average dystrophin protein level after 180 weeks of treatment with EXONDYS 51 was 0.93% of the dystrophin level in healthy subjects.

indication.text: Treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping; approved under accelerated approval based on an increase in dystrophin in skeletal muscle.

citations.quote: EXONDYS 51 is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping. This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on an increase in dystrophin in skeletal muscle observed in some patients treated with EXONDYS 51 [*see Clinical Studies (14)*]. target_moa.text: Eteplirsen binds to exon 51 of dystrophin pre-mRNA, causing exclusion of that exon during mRNA processing (exon skipping) so that an internally truncated but partially functional dystrophin protein can be produced in patients with mutations amenable to exon 51 skipping.

citations.quote: Etelirisen is designed to bind to exon 51 of dystrophin pre-mRNA, resulting in exclusion of this exon during mRNA processing in patients with genetic mutations that are amenable to exon 51 skipping. Exon skipping is intended to allow for production of an internally truncated dystrophin protein, which was evaluated in Study 2 and Study 3 [see Clinical studies (14)].

modality.text: Oligonucleotide — an antisense oligonucleotide of the phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) subclass.

citations.quote: Eteplirsen is an antisense oligonucleotide of the phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) subclass.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5% and higher than placebo) were balance disorder and vomiting. In Study 1, balance disorder occurred in 38% and vomiting in 38% of EXONDYS 51 patients (both 0% placebo), and contact dermatitis in 25% (0% placebo). Among 88 patients treated ≥30 mg/kg/week for up to 208 weeks, events in ≥10% and more frequent than in Study 1 included vomiting, contusion, excoriation, arthralgia, rash, catheter site pain, and upper respiratory tract infection.

vote.text: The application was presented to the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee on April 25, 2016. On the key vote on whether substantial evidence showed eteplirsen induces dystrophin to a level reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, the vote was 5 YES, 8 NO, 0 ABSTAIN.

requirement.text: PMR 3095-1: In order to verify the clinical benefit of eteplirsen, conduct a 2-year randomized, double-blind, controlled trial in patients with a confirmed DMD mutation amenable to exon 51 skipping, randomized to the approved 30 mg/kg weekly dosage or a significantly higher exposure (e.g., 30 mg/kg daily), with primary endpoint the North Star Ambulatory Assessment.

citations.quote: 3095-1 In order to verify the clinical benefit of etelprisen, conduct a 2-year randomized, double-blind, controlled trial of etelprisen in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 51 skipping. Patients should be randomized to the approved dosage of etelprisen (30 mg/kg weekly) or to a dosage that provides significantly higher exposure, e.g., 30 mg/kg daily. The primary endpoint will be the North Star Ambulatory Assessment.

requirement.text: PMR 3095-2: A two-year carcinogenicity study of intravenously administered eteplirsen in rat.

citations.quote: 3095-2 A two-year carcinogenicity study of intravenously administered etelplirsen in rat.

requirement.text: PMR 3095-4: A study to evaluate patient immune responses (IgM and IgG isotypes) to eteplirsen, its induced dystrophin, and full-length dystrophin, and the impact of immune responses on product PK, clinical efficacy and safety.

PMC 3095-5: Conduct a 2-year controlled trial in patients with a confirmed DMD mutation amenable to exon 45 or 53 skipping with a PMO designed to bind the corresponding exon splicing site, with primary objective of effect on the North Star Ambulatory Assessment.

citations.quote: 3095-5 Conduct a 2-year controlled trial in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 45 or 53 skipping with a phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) designed to bind to a regulatory site governing splicing of the corresponding exon.
